PullRequest.Title: refactor(sessions): move SessionsFlatList to sessionsFlatList.ts
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

## Why
This is the last move of phase 2, which splits the 11.5k-line `sessionsList.ts` into smaller modules. Stacked on #349663. The blocked-sessions dropdown and the automation run history only need the flat list, but they had to load the whole list control, `SessionsList`, to get it.

## What changed
- New `sessionsFlatList.ts` holds the Flat List region, copied byte for byte: `ISessionsFlatListOptions` and `SessionsFlatList`.
- Import lines in 5 files are updated, tests included, and the region is deleted from `sessionsList.ts`. Nothing is re-exported from there, and no `export` keyword needed adding.
- `blockedSessionsList.ts` and `automationRunHistory.ts` no longer import `sessionsList.ts`, directly or transitively. They still load `sessionsList.css` and `disclosure.css` through `sessionsListRenderers.ts`.

## Scope
No behavior changes. `sessionsList.ts` drops from 11,507 lines on main to 6,158 lines by the end of the stack.

## Blast Radius
Module load order only: the moved code has no module-level side effects, and there is no import cycle. The module evaluation order of every bundle entry point is unchanged.

## Verification
- Move check (a TypeScript compiler API script): 257/257 top-level declaration blocks are identical at base and head. The other 5 files changed only their import declarations.
- `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, `check-cyclic-dependencies`, and `oxlint` on the changed files all pass.
- Sessions list unit tests and the tests of its importers: 6,992 tests, the same count as base.
- Component fixtures for `sessionsList`, `sessionsListNotification`, `sessionsInboxScope`, and `blockedSessionsList`: 346/346 screenshots identical to base. Across all 2,247 `sessions/` fixtures, including the automations view, all screenshots match except a known flaky animation and one seeded-random fixture, explained in the comment.
- Bundled CSS (desktop, web, server-web, mobile): 6/6 files byte-identical.
- Code OSS Agents window, base and head: every grouping mode, Find, a context menu, drag and drop, and the blocked-sessions list give the same rows. Screenshots match pixel for pixel, and no new console errors appear.

Details in the first comment.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load the main sessions list, command-center dropdown code, and automation-history modules
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Module evaluation must finish before constructing these controls. The new file contains imports, an interface, and the same class declaration and decorators formerly evaluated in sessionsList.ts; it does not construct list instances or start provider requests at module scope.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One evaluation per distinct module in a module graph, not one evaluation per session or dropdown opening. Test files importing both controls now reference two modules.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous dependency evaluation; runtime service creation remains constructor-driven. Main-list imports no longer evaluate the flat-list declaration; flat-only consumers no longer directly load the main-list module.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Normal module caching preserves one class identity and one evaluation of shared renderer dependencies. Both controls still reach the same CSS through sessionsListRenderers.ts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete added/deleted class diff and all five importer diffs: implementation and runtime dependencies are moved, not duplicated into an additional instantiated control.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Bundle splitting and parse/evaluation timings were not measured. Their precise improvement or overhead cannot be inferred from source alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced performance regression. The changed imports narrow the flat-only dependency path without adding runtime initialization. No concrete prior regression symptom or introducing commit is established, so no regression-fix learning signal is submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, update, scroll, and close the ordinary or blocked command-center sessions dropdown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Construct one SessionsFlatList, set its sessions, compute content height, and synchronously lay out the embedded tree before showing the dropdown. Provider row-detail resolution is issued asynchronously and is not awaited by list display.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Observe rendered session resources and request optional provider detail resolution through $resolveChatSessionItem.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Ordinary preview contains at most eight sessions. Blocked input can be larger, but the viewport is capped at eight nominal rows. Cold requests scale with distinct rendered resources whose controllers support resolution, not every render; scrolling can expose additional resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same renderer, observeSession call, viewport limit, and provider controller caches were reached by SessionsFlatList in sessionsList.ts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget row enrichment; the dropdown does not await its completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive resolved item DTOs and look up chat metadata through the serialized store queue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One metadata lookup for a successful current-item resolution; unsupported controllers and cached resolutions issue no additional RPC. The index is cached, rather than reread from a file per row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical DTO conversion, metadata lookup, queue, and index cache before extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes provider enrichment, not initial dropdown visibility.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute aggregate row heights and lay out the tree following data and height changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Height calculation scales with supplied sessions; visible DOM is bounded by the dropdown viewport. Frequency and row-height callbacks are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deleted class contains identical setSessions, getContentHeight, layout, and height-change handling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous work on dropdown display and updates.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Up to eight ordinary preview sessions, or the distinct currently blocked sessions with an eight-row viewport; repeated dropdown updates and scrolling.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI layout is synchronous. Distinct cold row resolutions can run concurrently, while repeated requests for the same resource are suppressed/joined. Provider collection refreshes use existing per-provider throttled delayers. List, renderer templates, and subscriptions retain their existing disposal ownership.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: AgentSessionsModel guards each resource before issuing resolution. MainThreadChatSessions caches both completed and in-flight promises, returns immediately for unsupported resolution, and invalidates on item changes/removal. Errors delete the controller promise cache but do not create a new retry policy in this PR. Blocked dropdowns reuse the host approval model; ordinary previews own and dispose theirs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: constructor, rendering options, height work, cache reachability, and cleanup are unchanged across the complete move.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of blocked sessions and provider response times vary; no runtime measurements are available.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing collection scans, detail RPCs, synchronous layout, and resource lifetimes have identical multiplicity and scheduling before and after the diff.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display automation run history in the automations view or selected-automation modal, update live runs, and expand history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Read existing run/session snapshots, deduplicate continued sessions, select displayed runs, reuse date-group list blocks, and synchronously render/layout them. Provider refresh and row enrichment operate asynchronously outside this render pass.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve optional details for session rows actually presented in history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Initially ten history entries plus active/focused entries; Show More advances by twenty. Continued runs sharing a session are deduplicated. Requests scale with distinct displayed supported resources missing the shared resolution cache, not all runs or list blocks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same history selection, grouping, SessionsFlatList constructor, renderer, and resource-resolution caches.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reuse contiguous session-list blocks, update changed session arrays, read container width, and lay out lists to full content height.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One list per contiguous resolved-session block within a date group, not one list per run. An unchanged ordered session array skips setSessions and layout here. Existing height-change notifications can cause additional layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The extraction does not change block reuse, identity comparison, DOM reads/writes, or layout frequency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Background automation refresh delegates once to each provider automation store; stores may cross their existing host/network boundaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One refresh invocation per store per refresh cycle, not per displayed history entry. The view's scheduler runs sixty seconds after the existing refresh completes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same background scheduler, provider-store grouping, Promise.all delegation, and refresh placement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background refresh updates available snapshots; cached history can render without waiting.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Deduplicated run sessions, visible history page plus active/focused runs, date groups and unresolved-run separators, and available automation provider stores.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering/layout is synchronous. Cold detail requests are concurrent across distinct resources and coalesced per resource. Provider-store refreshes run through Promise.all; no new global limiter or additional burst is introduced. Metadata lookups use the existing serialized chat-store queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Persistent groups and list blocks are reused and disposed when removed. One approval model is shared across the section's lists. Identical session arrays suppress list reconstruction. Resource-resolution caches are shared across surfaces; controller errors and invalidation behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete move and inspected callers: pagination, session deduplication, grouping, equality suppression, service sharing, and cleanup retain the same implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Active run counts, provider-store internals, and network durations vary and were not profiled; none of their invocation counts or placement changes in this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced or materially amplified performance mechanism. Potential cost from large active histories or full-height list layout is pre-existing and outside this diff.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate a session row or use its contextual toolbar/menu actions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The moved onDidOpen and context-menu code dispatch the same callbacks. Opening waits for resource redirection and the existing session-opening path; automation history first resolves a missing resource before invoking its modal callback or sessionsService.openSession.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the selected session resource through providers, then open or reveal that session through existing services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected resource per activation. Providers supporting resource resolution are visited sequentially until one claims it. Automation history performs its preliminary resolution only when its local session lookup misses; sessionsService retains its own existing redirect check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical onDidOpen callback, mark-read condition, automation preliminary lookup, provider iteration, and session-opening calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resource resolution and opening are awaited on the selected-session navigation path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch explicit open-external or stop-cloud-run actions to existing opener/provider services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected run per action. Concurrent stop actions for the same run are suppressed by stoppingRuns; different run IDs can proceed independently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same action runner/callbacks and same per-run in-flight suppression.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the explicit action waits; menu creation itself does not issue these operations.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User activation frequency and eligible resource-resolution providers, not the total number of rows when merely opening a menu.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Resource-resolution providers are awaited sequentially for one activation. Existing session navigation cancellation and per-run stop suppression remain intact. The diff does not add parallel calls or an extra await.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing local session lookups avoid the automation history preliminary resolution on hits. Menu disposables remain scoped to menu hiding; no new cache or retained action state is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the complete moved event/action implementation is identical, and both production callers changed only their import source.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider redirect/open durations can be substantial, but exact timings and downstream implementation costs were not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the same expensive service operations occur for the same explicit actions, with unchanged ordering and cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all seven changed files and every diff page. SessionsFlatList's implementation is unchanged; only its module ownership and five importer declarations change. Investigated module evaluation, dropdown display/update/disposal, paginated and live automation history, shared row-resolution IPC and metadata queue caches, background provider refresh grouping, and explicit row actions. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying proven regression fix found. Static review; supporting guide delivery was tool-output truncated and no runtime profiling was performed.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
